subject: Can I apply calculateDiffMeth() to get differential methylated region after regionCount()?

messages.author: 0a5a875a96bb2f56
messages.subject: Can I apply calculateDiffMeth() to get differential methylated region after regionCount()?
parts:
Hi,

I've create an object describing the methylation status of interested region using regionCount(), the object looks like the following:

> head(regional_meth)

methylBase object with 6 rows
--------------
   chr   start     end strand id coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2 covered
1 chr1 3672548 3672697      -  1        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
2 chr1 3672547 3672696      -  2        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
3 chr1 3672546 3672695      -  3        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
4 chr1 3672545 3672694      -  4        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
5 chr1 3672544 3672693      -  5        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
6 chr1 3672543 3672692      -  6        30      1     29        21      0      21      3
   
--------------
sample.ids: Prom Gran 
destranded FALSE 
assembly: mm10 
context: CpG 
treament: 0 1 
resolution: region


Then I tried to apply calculateDiffMeth() to find differential methylated region and get the following result:

> regional_diff=calculateDiffMeth(regional_meth,num.cores = 6)
> head(regional_diff, 6)

methylDiff object with 6 rows
--------------
   chr   start     end strand pvalue qvalue  meth.diff
1 chr1 3672548 3672697      -      1      1 -2927.5862
2 chr1 3672547 3672696      -      1      1 -1427.5862
3 chr1 3672546 3672695      -      1      1  -927.5862
4 chr1 3672545 3672694      -      1      1  -677.5862
5 chr1 3672544 3672693      -      1      1  -527.5862
6 chr1 3672543 3672692      -      1      1  -427.5862
--------------
sample.ids: Prom Gran 
destranded FALSE 
assembly: mm10 
context: CpG 
treament: 0 1 
resolution: region


The values in "meth.diff" column looks so strange. 
So I wanna ask:
1) Why the "meth.diff" values are different for line 1 and 2? According to the first table, they have exact same coverage, numCs, numTs for both samples. 
2) How are those "meth.diff" values calculated? (I manually calculated the first one according to the first line in the regional_meth table, which equals 100*(0/21 - 1/30) = -3.33 ).  
3) Is there an alternative way to find differential methylated region using methylKit?

Thank you very much.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Can I apply calculateDiffMeth() to get differential methylated region after regionCount()?
parts:
the objects looks weird yes, there shouldn't be an "id" column in the methylBase object. I think this is a bug that occurs in regionCounts() when the first argument is a methylBase object. You can run regionCounts() on methylRawList then use unite() to get a methylBase object. I will fix this in the mean time and push it to the "development" version. I will let you know when it is ready.

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Can I apply calculateDiffMeth() to get differential methylated region after regionCount()?
parts:
This should be fixed in the development version, you can install it via install_github. Development version fixes a bunch of other issues from v0.9.2

https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/blob/development/NEWS

# dependencies
install.packages( c("data.table","devtools"))
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite(c("GenomicRanges","IRanges"))

# install the development version from github
library(devtools)
install_github("methylKit", username = "al2na",ref = "development")

On Friday, January 31, 2014 5:18:30 PM UTC+1, Altuna Akalin wrote:
the objects looks weird yes, there shouldn't be an "id" column in the methylBase object. I think this is a bug that occurs in regionCounts() when the first argument is a methylBase object. You can run regionCounts() on methylRawList then use unite() to get a methylBase object. I will fix this in the mean time and push it to the "development" version. I will let you know when it is ready.

Best,
Altuna
